title: What If Computers Ran Out of Time in 2038?

scenes.text: What if computers ran out of time? It happens on January nineteenth, twenty thirty-eight.
Older computers count seconds since nineteen seventy in a number that maxes out near two point one billion.
At three fourteen and seven seconds UTC that morning, the counter hits its limit.
One second later it flips negative, and the clock jumps back to December thirteenth, nineteen oh one.
Older embedded systems, some file systems and some thirty-two-bit devices could break. Logs, certificates and timers too.
Sixty-four-bit time lasts about two hundred ninety-two billion years. The hard part is finding every old machine still running.

description:
What if computers ran out of time?
On 19 January 2038 a 32-bit time counter overflows and old systems think it is 1901. The fix exists: 64-bit time lasts about 292 billion years.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Do you still have a 32-bit gadget in a drawer? What should we run through next?
